welcome.title: Let Agents Connect Securely
welcome.lede:
Let Grok Bot and Muse in the cloud use Claude Code and Codex on your computer,
and give specialist tasks to specialist agents.
welcome.promise: Even if the server is breached, attackers can’t reach your computer. Sessions are end-to-end encrypted; the server can’t see what’s in them.

browser.title: Complete Sign-In in Your Browser
browser.body: You’ll come back here on your own when you’re done. Signing in the first time creates your account; no password needed.

selfHosted.title: Connect Your Own Server
selfHosted.body: Enter the address of the Hermesh server you deployed, and the claim code it gave when it first started.
selfHosted.join: Already using Hermesh on another device? <join>Join it…</join>

joinAddress.invalid: That address isn’t right: it should look like relay.example.com/o_xxxxxxxx
joinAddress.title: Join Your Existing Hermesh
joinAddress.body: The connection address is in Hermesh on a device you already have: Settings › Trusted Devices.

authorize.joinNote: After you continue, use Touch ID once, then approve on your existing device.
authorize.machineOnlyNote: No Touch ID needed: approve on your existing device.
authorize.titleJoin: Add This Mac to Your Hermesh?
authorize.titleTrust: Make This Mac Your Trusted Device?
authorize.body: This is all Hermesh does: it doesn’t change system settings or read your files.
authorize.trustedBody: Creates your owner key in this Mac’s security chip; it never leaves this Mac. From then on, when machines and agents want to connect to your computer, you approve with Touch ID here.
authorize.trustedOff: Off: no owner key here. This Mac only runs tasks: it approves nothing and doesn’t see your other machines. For a work Mac, say.
authorize.shareBody: Hermesh uses Claude Code and Codex on this Mac from the command line, just as you do. It doesn’t read API keys or tokens, or touch these agents’ sign-ins. Off, you can still use other machines; you can turn it on later in Settings.
authorize.shareBodyMachine: Hermesh uses Claude Code and Codex on this Mac from the command line, just as you do. It doesn’t read API keys or tokens, or touch these agents’ sign-ins.
authorize.remind: Remind me when something comes up
authorize.remindBody: Open Hermesh at login (in the menu bar only). Notify me of connection requests, agent questions and failed sessions.
authorize.remindBodyMachine: Open Hermesh at login (in the menu bar only). Notify me when a session fails.

join.expired: The join request expired. Please join again.
join.wrongDigits: Those digits are wrong. Enter the two digits shown on your other device.
join.titleDigits: Enter the Two Digits on That Device
join.waiting: Open Hermesh on your existing device and approve this Mac’s join request.
join.waitingMachine: Open Hermesh on your existing device and approve this Mac joining as a machine.
join.codeHint: Must match what that device shows
join.approved: “{{name}}” approved. It now shows two digits; enter them:
join.notMeNote: No digits on that device? Then you didn’t make this approval; click “I Didn’t Approve This”.
join.notMeNoteMachine: No digits on that device? If its Hermesh isn’t the latest version, update it, then click “I Didn’t Approve This” and join again. If it is and there are still none, you didn’t make this approval.

unreachable.title: Can’t Reach the Hermesh Server
unreachable.body: This network may be blocking {{host}}, as company networks and proxies often do. Try another network, such as your phone’s hotspot. Nothing on this Mac has changed yet.

removed.title: This Mac Is No Longer in Your Hermesh Account
removed.body: Another of your devices removed it, or the account started over. This Mac can no longer approve anything. Set it up again to rejoin your account.
removed.bodyMachine: It was removed from your machines, or the account started over. It takes no more tasks. Set it up again to rejoin your account.

machineOnly.leaveMessage: This Mac stops taking tasks at once, and turns under way stop. It leaves your machine list too (if it can’t reach the server now, remove it there from a trusted device). Its projects stay here.

connect.promise: Once approved, it gets access you signed and connects straight to your computer with its own key, end-to-end encrypted; the server sees none of it.

firstTask.title: “{{name}}” Is Connected
firstTask.tryIt: Try it in {{name}}: send it this:
firstTask.waiting: As soon as it starts working, its session opens here.
firstTask.promptInProject: Use Hermesh to have {{agent}} say hello to me in the {{project}} project.
firstTask.prompt: Use Hermesh to have {{agent}} say hello to me.

prepare.promise: Never takes any agent’s tokens or keys; uses them only as you would on the command line.
prepare.title: Check and Manage Available Agents
prepare.searching: Looking for Coding Agents on This Mac
prepare.searchingBody: Checking which ones are installed, their versions and whether you’re signed in. The first check takes a moment.
prepare.notInstalled: Not installed · Hermesh finds them once they are
prepare.waitingLogin: Waiting for you to sign in in Terminal…
prepare.loginFirst: Sign in to {{agent}} first so Hermesh can use it.
prepare.otherProjects: Other projects · for agents not installed
prepare.worktreeItem: Separate Worktree: Each Session on Its Own Branch
prepare.inPlaceItem: In Place: Change This Folder Directly
prepare.defaultsNote: Sessions an agent starts here without naming a model use these. {{agent}}’s own settings stay as they are.

why.appWithoutCli: {{app}} is installed, but not {{agent}}’s command line tool, which Hermesh runs. Install it as {{agent}}’s documentation says; Hermesh finds it by itself.
why.noProcesses: Found, but it can’t start: this machine can’t start new programs (out of processes).
why.timedOut: Found {{binary}}, but it didn’t answer within 20 seconds. Run it in Terminal to see whether it hangs.
why.missingRuntime: Found {{binary}}, but {{runtime}}, which runs it, can’t be found. Make sure it runs in Terminal.

erased.by: You erased everything in Hermesh on “{{device}}”
erased.byBody: Hermesh on this Mac is erased too.
erased.pending: {{names}} were offline: reset or pair each again when you next use it.
